_about: Editorial layer for /guides/best-resume-tools. Numbers never live here: ratings, prices and scores come from lib/scorecards/resume-tools.json, other reviewers from benchmarks.json, videos from videos.json. call.stance: agrees (we land where current lists land) | breaks (we land somewhere else, and say why) | thin (not enough evidence for anyone to rank it). call lines are drafts until the founder marks them up (callsReviewed).

refreshLog.what: Ratings, review counts, prices and traffic ranks
Other reviewers' lists and demo videos added
refreshLog.how: Gathered from search listings. Confirmed on the live pages at the next monthly check.

picks.label: Best overall
picks.line: Checker, builder, and job tracker in one, with a real free tier.

picks.label: Best truly free
picks.line: The only builder here with genuinely free, watermark-free PDF downloads.

picks.label: Best paid builder
picks.line: Honest annual pricing at $96, and students get six months free.

teal.bestFor: Checker, builder, and tracker in one. Real free tier

call.line: Three current lists name Teal, and we rank it first too. The reason is boring and rare: the free tier is a real product.

verdict.bestIf: You want one tool for the whole search: resume builder, per-job keyword matching, and application tracking. The free tier is a real product, and 200,000 Chrome users rate it 4.9.
verdict.skipIf: You only need one deep scan against one job description. Jobscan's per-job reports go further.
verdict.like: Free tier that does not hold your resume hostage. Quarterly billing at $79 is the sane paid option.
verdict.watch: The $13 weekly plan reads cheap and compounds fast. Pick monthly or quarterly, never weekly.

call.line: The current lists put Jobscan near the top for per-job matching, and so do we. Use the report, ignore the score.

resume-worded.bestFor: Instant free score; the fixes cost $49/mo

call.line: One list names it, and that list is about three years old. With 9 citable reviews, nobody has enough evidence to rank it, us included.

kickresume.bestFor: Best paid builder. Templates recruiters read

call.line: Zapier picks it and so do we. $96 a year is the whole price, which in this category counts as a feature.

verdict.bestIf: You want a polished paid builder without billing games: $96 a year, flat, with 6,400 mobile ratings averaging 4.6 to back it up.
verdict.skipIf: FlowCV's free tier already covers you. Pay for a builder only when you need multiple tailored versions.
verdict.like: Free tier allows real downloads on basic templates. Students get six months of premium free with a student ID.
verdict.watch: Web and iOS pricing differ; the App Store subscription is cheaper. Check both before paying.

flowcv.bestFor: The genuinely free builder. No watermark

call.line: No current list we track names FlowCV. We rank it the best free builder anyway: it is the only one here that hands you a clean PDF for nothing.
Only a 2024 list mentions Rezi. We rank it third of seven builders for ATS-first formatting and a $149 lifetime plan that never renews.

rezi.pricingLine: 1 resume and 3 PDFs free · $29/mo or $149 lifetime

resume-io.bestFor: Polished editor behind a billing trap

call.line: Zapier picks Resume.io. We rank it fourth of seven: the $2.95 trial renews at $29.95 every 4 weeks, and creators are now posting how-to-cancel videos.

verdict.bestIf: You want the slickest editor in the category, you set a calendar reminder to cancel, and you treat it as a $2.95 one-week rental.
verdict.skipIf: You might forget to cancel. The trial renews at $29.95 every 4 weeks, 13 times a year, and the free download is plain text with your formatting stripped.
verdict.like: The editor itself is genuinely good, which is what makes the billing model such a shame.
verdict.watch: Its only citable public review base is 1.5 out of 5 across 195 Product Hunt reviews, nearly all about the renewal pattern. The App Store apps under this name are third-party lookalikes, not Resume.io.

resume-io.pricingLine: $2.95 7-day trial, renews $29.95 every 4 weeks · free download is .txt only

call.line: No current list we track names it, and it has 1 citable review. No free plan, and the trial watermarks your download.

enhancv.pricingLine: 7-day watermarked trial · from about $13.33/mo on 6-month billing

call.line: No current list we track names it, and there are no citable reviews to score yet.
Zety's strongest placements are on lists owned by its own parent company, BOLD. We show those lists and don't count them. On the evidence we do count, it doesn't earn a rank.

zety.pricingLine: $1.95 trial, renews $25.95 every 4 weeks · free download is .txt only
